speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your systemic hypertension; can you tell me your age and if you have noticed any headaches, vision changes, or chest pain? REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel, Urinalysis, and Lipid Panel.

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the finding of high blood pressure specifically on the right upper extremity is concerning for a coarctation of the aorta. Can you tell me if you have noticed coldness, color changes, or weak pulses in your legs or feet? REQUEST TEST: Upper and Lower Extremity Blood Pressure Measurement; REQUEST TEST: Upper and Lower Extremity Pulse Palpation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Pressure: 150/80 mm Hg (Right Upper Extremity); Pulses: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The significant discrepancy between your right upper extremity blood pressure and the trace femoral pulses strongly suggests obstruction in the aorta. Can you tell me if you have noticed any pain in your abdomen, buttocks, or legs, or if you experience difficulty running or walking? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound; REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram and Aortic Angiography.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram Findings: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta. The clinical presentation of right upper extremity hypertension, weak femoral pulses, and the echocardiogram showing aortic narrowing distal to the left subclavian artery confirms this diagnosis.
